# ADaM Reviewer's Guide {#sec-appendix-adrg}

This appendix describes the analysis datasets behind this report, in the spirit of a CDISC ADaM Reviewer's Guide (ADRG): each dataset's structure, its key derived variables, and the population flags used to select analysis subsets.
It is a narrative companion to the metadata excerpt in @sec-reproducibility, not a substitute for it.

## Dataset overview

```{r}
#| label: adrg-overview

tibble::tribble(
  ~Dataset, ~Structure, ~`Key derived variables`,
  "ADSL", "One record per subject", "TRT01P/TRT01A, SAFFL, ITTFL, PPROTFL, COMPFL, AGEGR1",
  "ADAE", "One record per subject per adverse event", "TRTEMFL (subset to TRUE), RELFL, DERMFL",
  "ADEX", "One record per subject", "AVAL (total exposure days), derived from EX",
  "ADLB", "One record per subject per lab test per visit", "BNRIND, ANRIND (reference-range indicators)",
  "ADTTE", "One record per subject per time-to-event parameter", "AVAL, CNSR, derived with admiral::derive_param_tte()",
  "ADVS", "One record per subject per vital-signs test per visit", "BNRIND, ANRIND (reference-range indicators)"
) |>
  gt_nordvale() |>
  gt::tab_header(title = gt::md("Analysis datasets used in this report"))
```

All six datasets derive from the CDISC pilot study (`CDISCPILOT01`) shipped in `pharmaverseadam`, restricted in `R/00-adam.R` to the three randomised treatment arms.
ADTTE is not shipped by `pharmaverseadam` and is derived from ADSL and ADAE.

## ADSL: Subject-level analysis dataset

ADSL carries one record per randomised subject and the population flags that select analysis subsets throughout this report:

- `SAFFL`: safety population, subjects who received at least one dose of study drug.
- `ITTFL`: intention-to-treat population; every randomised subject is `"Y"`, since all received the assigned treatment.
- `PPROTFL`: per-protocol population, approximated as safety-population subjects who completed the study, because no protocol deviation data ship with the pilot study.
- `COMPFL`: completers, derived from `EOSSTT == "COMPLETED"`.

`TRT01P` and `TRT01A` (planned and actual treatment for period 01) drive every by-treatment column in this report; they agree for every subject, since no subject crossed over between arms.

## ADAE: Adverse events analysis dataset

ADAE is restricted to treatment-emergent events (`TRTEMFL == "Y"`) reported by safety-population subjects.
Two flags derived in `R/00-adam.R` are used beyond the standard ADaM variables:

- `RELFL`: related to study drug, derived from `AEREL %in% c("PROBABLE", "POSSIBLE", "RELATED")`.
- `DERMFL`: dermatologic event, derived from `AEBODSYS == "SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS"`; this flag identifies the events contributing to the primary endpoint.

## ADEX: Exposure analysis dataset

ADEX carries one record per subject with total exposure duration (`AVAL`, parameter `TDURD`), restricted to the safety population.
Table 14.3.1 in the safety evaluation chapter draws directly from this dataset without further derivation.

## ADLB and ADVS: Laboratory and vital-signs analysis datasets

ADLB and ADVS share the same structure: one record per subject per test per visit, restricted to the safety population, with a baseline reference-range indicator (`BNRIND`) carried onto every post-baseline record alongside that record's own indicator (`ANRIND`).
This shared structure is what lets `R/tlf.R`'s `tlf_shift()` compute shift-from-baseline tables (Tables 14.3.6 through 14.3.8) identically for both domains, keyed only by `PARAM`.

## ADTTE: Time-to-event analysis dataset

ADTTE is derived, not sourced, since `pharmaverseadam` does not ship a time-to-event dataset for this study.
`R/00-adam.R` builds it with `admiral::derive_param_tte()` from two sources:

- An event source, the first dermatologic treatment-emergent adverse event per subject (`ASTDT`, one row per subject via `slice_min()`).
- A censoring source, the subject's last date known to be alive (`LSTALVDT`), for subjects without a qualifying event.

`AVAL` is the resulting time to event in days, and `CNSR` distinguishes events (`0`) from censoring (`1`).
`TRT01P`, `TRT01A`, `SAFFL`, `PPROTFL`, `AGE`, `AGEGR1` and `SEX` are merged back from ADSL so that the primary and supportive analyses in the primary and secondary endpoints chapter need no further joins.
